title: En passant

D0.outcome: Describes en passant: when an enemy pawn moves two squares past your pawn you may capture it on the very next move as if it had moved one square.

D1.outcome: When told 'capture en passant', does it, for both colours.

D2.outcome: Decides whether en passant is possible right now, and lists a pawn's moves including the en passant capture.

D3.outcome: Notices when an en passant capture would expose its own king, and decides whether the capture is legal.

misconceptions: En passant can be played any time later.
Any pawn standing beside an enemy pawn can capture it en passant.
The capturing pawn lands on the square of the pawn it captures.
conditions: It is possible only on the move right after an enemy pawn advanced two squares and landed beside your pawn.
The capturing pawn goes to the square the enemy pawn passed over, and the enemy pawn is removed.
contrasts: A pawn that reached the square beside yours earlier, or by single steps, cannot be captured en passant.
What the enemy moved before the last move does not matter; only the last move counts.
